title: Lattice
tagline: One beam, and everything you own is a mirror.
description: Tower defence with nothing to shoot with. There is a single light source, fixed where it is, and you cannot add another or make it stronger. What you can do is place mirrors, splitters, prisms, filters and lenses to steer that one beam along the lane the shades walk down. The shades resist colours: a crimson one takes nothing at all from red light, so somewhere in your layout there has to be a prism splitting white apart and the right colour arriving in the right place. Eight maps, each one proved winnable with the optics it gives you.
author: HexCave
controls: Tap a placed optic to rotate
howToPlay: Pick an optic from the tray, then click or tap an empty square to place it. Keys 1 to 5 also select.
Click a placed optic to rotate it. Right-click, or the remove tool, takes it back and refunds its cost.
A mirror turns the beam ninety degrees, a splitter sends it two ways, a prism breaks white into red, green and blue, a filter keeps one colour, and a lens doubles whatever passes through.
You may build in the lane itself — shades are shadows and walk straight through your glass. Running the beam along the lane is usually the whole idea.
Shades resist one or two colours and take nothing from those. White light carries all three, so splitting it and routing the parts is what beats the resistant ones.
Press start when the layout is ready. Anything that reaches the far end costs you a life, and you can rebuild between waves.
goal: Stop every wave before it reaches the far end. You have a fixed budget of optics per map and no way to buy more damage.

1.0.0.notes: First release. Eight maps, each proved winnable within its budget.
